Q: Algorithm ai cannot solve A:

Well, there's a bunch of examples of similar fails where a model just happily starts pumping out text until it hits a limit, so if you're looking for any one reason why it could be expected to happen, then "because it's happened before" is one.

It's not guaranteed of course, if a model is trained to specifically give good answers to tasks with such a catch, it probably will. Retraining to correctly solve famous catches is common. I've also seen models trained with a badly designed objective of "just shorten it" which discards the condition of no loops, failing this task... a correct answer is "point out that it's impossible because the output would be too long".

Q: Migrating from log4j 1.x to log4j 2 : Stack trace format A:

The ~[bin/:?] is packaging information added by the xEx pattern converter (cf. documentation). It includes information about the JAR that contains the class:

At the end of each stack element of the exception, a string containing the name of the jar file that contains the class or the directory the class is located in and the "Implementation-Version" as found in that jar's manifest will be added. If the information is uncertain, then the class packaging data will be preceded by a tilde, i.e. the ~ character.

Your code isn't packaged yet, so you get ~[bin/:?].

If you want a "standard" stacktrace, add %n%ex at the end of your pattern.

Edit: since Log4j Core 2.25.0, the default pattern converter for exceptions was changed from %xEx to %ex, so packaging information will no longer show in stack traces by default.

Q: When using nginx, how do i limit the requests per seconds in total to the upstream? A:

You can use the key $server_name in limit_req_zone to limit the requests for the whole server.
